Imperial Secretary Chen Qiao said, "The King died away from the capital, and the realm is filled with fear.
尚書 is an Imperial Secretary (Master of Writing); the literal draft wrongly renders it "Minister of Works".
The reign era was changed to Yancong.
The reign era was changed to Yankang.
延康 is romanized Yankang; the draft misspells it "Yancong".
Palace Attendant Sima Fu admonished him: "Our lord is gone, and the empire looks to Your Highness for its very life.
Palace Cadet Sima Fu admonished him: "Our lord is gone, and the empire looks to Your Highness for its very life.
中庶子 is the Crown Prince's Palace Cadet, not a "Palace Attendant".

Li Fu, Left Commandant of the Center, and Xu Zhi, assistant director of the Astronomical Bureau, submitted a memorial: "Wei is destined to replace Han, as charts and prophetic texts show—and the evidence is abundant."

Li Fu, General of the Household of the Left, and Xu Zhi, assistant director of the Astronomical Bureau, submitted a memorial: "Wei is destined to replace Han, as charts and prophetic texts show—and the evidence is abundant."
左中郎將 is General of the Household of the Left; the draft's literal "Left Commandant of the Center" is wrong.

Meng Da was a man of fine presence and ability, and the King held him in high regard, taking him into his own carriage. He appointed Da Attendant Cavalier and General Who Establishes Might and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pingyang.

Meng Da was a man of fine presence and ability, and the King held him in high regard, taking him into his own carriage. He appointed Da Attendant Cavalier and General Who Establishes Might and enfeoffed him as Village Marquis of Pingyang.
平陽亭侯 is a village (亭) marquisate; the draft drops the rank and renders it simply "Marquis of Pingyang".
The Emperor summoned Jiang Ji, Eastern Commandant of the Center, to serve as Attendant Cavalier.
The Emperor summoned Jiang Ji, General of the Household of the East, to serve as Attendant Cavalier.
東中郎將 is General of the Household of the East; the draft's literal "Eastern Commandant of the Center" is wrong.
In spring, the first month, Proposal Gentleman Kong Xian was appointed Marquis Who Honors the Sage to preside over sacrifices to Confucius.
In spring, the first month, Court Gentleman for Consultation Kong Xian was appointed Marquis Who Honors the Sage to preside over sacrifices to Confucius.
議郎 is Court Gentleman for Consultation; the draft's literal "Proposal Gentleman" is an error.
End editorial note. to record the affairs of the various states—not to honor one and demean another, nor to draw orthodox-intercalary distinctions.

Because Han passed the throne to Wei and Jin received it, Jin passed it to Song and on to Chen before Sui took it, and Tang passed it to Liang and on to Zhou before the Great Song inherited it, I cannot avoid using the era names of Wei, Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Later Liang, Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han and Later Zhou to record the affairs of the various states—not to honor one and demean another, nor to draw orthodox-intercalary distinctions.

The draft drops the whole first half of the sentence (the succession Han–Wei–Jin–Song–Chen–Sui–Tang–Liang–Zhou–Song and the list of era names used) and inserts a stray "End editorial note."; the literal field is truncated the same way.
The empress was the younger sister of General of the Left Yi and the former wife of Liu Zhang's elder brother Mao.
The empress was the younger sister of Lieutenant General Yi and the former wife of Liu Zhang's elder brother Mao.
偏將軍 is Lieutenant General, not "General of the Left".

When the Grand Ancestor entered Ye, the Emperor was Commandant of the Five Offices of the Center; he saw Yuan Xi's wife, Lady Zhen of Zhongshan, was beautiful and was pleased with her; the Grand Ancestor arranged the betrothal for him, and she bore a son, Rui.

When the Grand Ancestor entered Ye, the Emperor was General of the Household for All Purposes; he saw Yuan Xi's wife, Lady Zhen of Zhongshan, was beautiful and was pleased with her; the Grand Ancestor arranged the betrothal for him, and she bore a son, Rui.
五官中郎將 is General of the Household for All Purposes (Leader of Court Gentlemen of the Five Offices); the draft's "Commandant of the Five Offices of the Center" is wrong.

Quan made General Who Pacifies the West Lu Xun grand commander with provisional credentials and put him in command of Generals Zhu Ran, Pan Zhang, Song Qian, Han Dang, Xu Sheng, Xianyu Dan, Sun Huan, and others—fifty thousand men—to resist them.

Quan made General Who Guards the West Lu Xun grand commander with provisional credentials and put him in command of Generals Zhu Ran, Pan Zhang, Song Qian, Han Dang, Xu Sheng, Xianyu Dan, Sun Huan, and others—fifty thousand men—to resist them.
鎮西將軍 is General Who Guards the West; "Pacifies" renders 平/安, not 鎮.
Quan may have heroic talent, but he is merely the former Han Cavalry General and Marquis of Nanchang—a title light in rank and low in prestige.
Quan may have heroic talent, but he is merely the former Han General of Swift Cavalry and Marquis of Nanchang—a title light in rank and low in prestige.
票騎將軍 (=驃騎將軍) is General of Swift Cavalry, a top-rank generalship; the draft flattens it to "Cavalry General" (the source here also has the scribal variant 帆軍 for 將軍).
The generals, seeing Wu submit from within, all relaxed their guard; only General Who Subdues the South Xiahou Shang further strengthened offensive and defensive preparations.
The generals, seeing Wu submit from within, all relaxed their guard; only Grand General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang further strengthened offensive and defensive preparations.
征南大將軍 is Grand General Who Conquers the South; the draft drops 大 and mistranslates 征.

Central Palace Gentleman Xu Sheng of Langye, resentful and indignant, turned to his fellows and said: "We could not exert ourselves and give our lives, unite Xu and Luo for the state, swallow Ba and Shu—and now we make our lord ally with Zhen—is this not shame!"

General of the Household Xu Sheng of Langye, resentful and indignant, turned to his fellows and said: "We could not exert ourselves and give our lives, unite Xu and Luo for the state, swallow Ba and Shu—and now we make our lord ally with Zhen—is this not shame!"
中郎將 is General of the Household; the draft's literal "Central Palace Gentleman" is wrong.

The King of Wu made his son Deng crown prince and finely selected teachers and companions—making Zhuge Ke, son of Grand Administrator of Nanjun Zhuge Jin; Sun Xiu, son of General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhang Zhao; Gu Tan, son of Grand Judge of Wujun Gu Yong; and Chen Biao, son of Adjunct General of Lujiang Chen Wu all Supernumerary Palace Attendants. They entered to lecture on the Poetry and Documents and went out to follow in horsemanship and archery—he called them the Four Friends.

The King of Wu made his son Deng crown prince and finely selected teachers and companions—making Zhuge Ke, son of Grand Administrator of Nanjun Zhuge Jin; Zhang Xiu, son of General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhang Zhao; Gu Tan, son of Grand Judge of Wujun Gu Yong; and Chen Biao, son of Adjunct General of Lujiang Chen Wu all Palace Cadets. They entered to lecture on the Poetry and Documents and went out to follow in horsemanship and archery—he called them the Four Friends.
張昭之子休 is Zhang Xiu (Zhang Zhao's son), not "Sun Xiu"; and 中庶子 is Palace Cadet, not "Supernumerary Palace Attendant".
The Han ruler refused and instead made Huang Quan General Who Pacifies the North, assigning him to command all forces north of the Yangtze;
The Han ruler refused and instead made Huang Quan General Who Guards the North, assigning him to command all forces north of the Yangtze;
鎮北將軍 is General Who Guards the North; "Pacifies" renders 平/安, not 鎮.
only the Prince of Beihai, Cao Tan, was conscientious and studious and never gave cause for complaint.
only the Prince of Beihai, Cao Gun, was conscientious and studious and never gave cause for complaint.
兗 here is Cao Gun (曹袞, also written 兗), Prince of Beihai; the draft wrongly renders him "Cao Tan".
They jointly submitted a memorial praising Cao Tan's merit.
They jointly submitted a memorial praising Cao Gun's merit.
兗 is Cao Gun (曹袞); the draft wrongly renders "Cao Tan".
Cao Tan, hearing of this, was greatly alarmed and rebuked the literary attendants: "Self-cultivation is ordinary conduct; yet you report it to the throne—you only increase my burden thereby.
Cao Gun, hearing of this, was greatly alarmed and rebuked the literary attendants: "Self-cultivation is ordinary conduct; yet you report it to the throne—you only increase my burden thereby.
兗 is Cao Gun (曹袞); the draft wrongly renders "Cao Tan".

Earlier, Sun Huan, Central Guard General of Andong under Wu, had attacked the Han vanguard separately at Yidao and been surrounded by Han forces. He appealed to Lu Xun for relief. Xun said: "Not yet."

Earlier, Sun Huan, General of the Household Who Pacifies the East under Wu, had attacked the Han vanguard separately at Yidao and been surrounded by Han forces. He appealed to Lu Xun for relief. Xun said: "Not yet."
安東中郎將 is General of the Household Who Pacifies the East; the draft misreads 安東 as a place "Andong" and 中郎將 as "Central Guard General".
The King laughed and praised him. Lu Xun was promoted to Assistant State General, made Governor of Jing Province, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangling.
The King laughed and praised him. Lu Xun was promoted to General Who Supports the State, made Governor of Jing Province, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangling.
輔國將軍 is General Who Supports the State; "Assistant State General" is a literal error.
In the twelfth year, in the seventh month of autumn, Jizhou suffered a plague of locusts and famine.
In autumn, in the seventh month, Jizhou suffered a plague of locusts and famine.
The source has only 秋，七月; the draft inserts a spurious "In the twelfth year".
In the thirteenth year, after the Han ruler's defeat and flight, Huang Quan was stranded north of the river with his escape cut off. In the eighth month he led his troops to surrender.
After the Han ruler's defeat and flight, Huang Quan was stranded north of the river with his escape cut off. In the eighth month he led his troops to surrender.
The source has no year number here; the draft inserts a spurious ordinal year ("In the thirteenth year").
In the fourteenth year, on the day Jiawu in the ninth month, an edict declared: "When women take part in government, disorder follows.
On the day Jiawu in the ninth month, an edict declared: "When women take part in government, disorder follows.
The source has no year number here; the draft inserts a spurious ordinal year ("In the fourteenth year").

In the fifteenth year, when the Emperor was about to install Honored Consort Guo as empress, Palace Gentleman Zhan Qian submitted a memorial: "The character of empress and consort is the source from which a state's rise and fall, order and chaos, proceed.

When the Emperor was about to install Honored Consort Guo as empress, Palace Gentleman Zhan Qian submitted a memorial: "The character of empress and consort is the source from which a state's rise and fall, order and chaos, proceed.
The source has no year number here; the draft inserts a spurious ordinal year ("In the fifteenth year").
In the sixteenth year, the King of Wu sent Protector of the Army Hao Zhou and Army Major Dongli Gun to the Emperor, declaring his sincere submission in language of deep respect and earnest devotion.
Earlier, the King of Wu sent Protector of the Army Hao Zhou and Army Major Dongli Gun to the Emperor, declaring his sincere submission in language of deep respect and earnest devotion.
The source has no year number here; the draft inserts a spurious ordinal year ("In the sixteenth year"). 初 means "earlier".

In the seventeenth year, on the day Jiazi in the tenth month of winter, he designated the eastern slope of Mount Shouyang as the site of the Shou Mausoleum and wrote his final instructions, insisting on thrift: no gold or jade for burial, only earthenware vessels.

On the day Jiazi in the tenth month of winter, he designated the eastern slope of Mount Shouyang as the site of the Shou Mausoleum and wrote his final instructions, insisting on thrift: no gold or jade for burial, only earthenware vessels.
The source has no year number here; the draft inserts a spurious ordinal year ("In the seventeenth year").
In the eighteenth year, because many of the Yang-Yue tribal peoples had not yet been pacified, the King of Wu wrote humbly to the Emperor, pledging to reform himself;
Because many of the Yang-Yue tribal peoples had not yet been pacified, the King of Wu wrote humbly to the Emperor, pledging to reform himself;
The source has no year number here; the draft inserts a spurious ordinal year ("In the eighteenth year").
The Emperor said to Huang Quan: "You have abandoned the rebel cause and come over to us. Do you wish to emulate Chen She and Han Xin?"
The Emperor said to Huang Quan: "You have abandoned the rebel cause and come over to us. Do you wish to emulate Chen Ping and Han Xin?"
陳、韓 refers to Chen Ping and Han Xin, who deserted Xiang Yu for Liu Bang; Chen She was a rebel, not a defector.
The Emperor was pleased and appointed Huang Quan Pacifying South General, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuyang, made him Palace Attendant, and had him ride in the imperial escort chariot.
The Emperor was pleased and appointed Huang Quan General Who Guards the South, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuyang, made him Palace Attendant, and had him ride in the imperial escort chariot.
鎮南將軍 is General Who Guards the South; "Pacifying" renders 平/安, not 鎮.

Wu's Establishing Prestige General Lu Fan commanded five armies and met Cao Xiu's forces with the navy. Left General Zhuge Jin, Pacifying North General Pan Zhang, and General Yang Can marched to relieve Nan Commandery. Vice General Zhu Huan, as Supervisor of Ruxu, held Cao Ren at bay.

Wu's Establishing Prestige General Lü Fan commanded five armies and met Cao Xiu's forces with the navy. Left General Zhuge Jin, Pacifying North General Pan Zhang, and General Yang Can marched to relieve Nan Commandery. Vice General Zhu Huan, as Supervisor of Ruxu, held Cao Ren at bay.
呂範 is Lü Fan (as the draft itself writes in s0606); "Lu Fan" drops the umlaut.
The King of Wu sent Grand Palace Attendant Zheng Quan on a mission to Han; Han Grand Palace Attendant Zong Wei replied in turn, and Wu and Han restored diplomatic contact.
The King of Wu sent Grand Master of the Palace Zheng Quan on a mission to Han; Han Grand Master of the Palace Zong Wei replied in turn, and Wu and Han restored diplomatic contact.
太中大夫 is Grand Master of the Palace (as the draft renders it in s0042), not "Grand Palace Attendant".
